panels.title: Who was Pliny?
points: He watched from across the bay
Years later he wrote letters about it

passage.title: Pliny the Younger, letter to Tacitus about AD 79, adapted for Year 3 by the teacher
paras: A great cloud was rising from a mountain. Its shape was like a pine tree: it shot up high on a tall trunk and then spread out into branches. Sometimes it was white, sometimes dark and patchy. Later, ash began to fall on us, and darkness came, blacker than any night.

keywords.def: a person who saw something happen with their own eyes
the feeling or mood of a piece of writing

questions.q: Why does Pliny say 'blacker than any night'?
questions.a: to show the darkness was worse than anything he knew

questions.q: Core: collect five powerful words or phrases and write what each makes you picture
Extend: write two sentences: why is Pliny's account powerful?
questions.a: For example: He saw it himself, so his details are real. His comparisons help us picture it.

questions.q: Stretch: write a simile of your own about the ash cloud
questions.a: For example: The ash fell like grey snow.

questions.q: What did Pliny compare the cloud to?
questions.a: B) a pine tree. He said it rose on a tall trunk and spread into branches, like a pine tree.

questions.q: Write one powerful word from today
